responses.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_rental_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_rate_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) t

assumptions.assumption: Films with NULL rating (none expected, since all films fall in the 5 verified levels) would form their own group; the query does not exclude them. Ratio is computed per film as rental_rate / replacement_cost (decimal division, unrounded), then averaged within each rating, then averaged across ratings with equal weight.

assumptions.assumption: Ratings with NULL rating are not expected (5 rating levels verified); any NULL rating group would be treated as its own group by GROUP BY. replacement_cost is NOT NULL so the filter is straightforward, and the ratio is computed per film as rental_rate / replacement_cost before averaging within each rating.

responses.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_dur) AS avg_of_avg_duration, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratio FROM (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_dur, AVG(rental_rate / replacement_cost) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating) t

assumptions.assumption: Films with a NULL rating (if any) would form their own group; the verified data shows exactly 5 rating levels, so this should not matter. replacement_cost is NOT NULL, so no division-by-zero or missing-ratio concerns beyond AVG ignoring NULLs.
The ratio is computed per film (rental_rate / replacement_cost) and then averaged within each rating, not as a ratio of averages.
